Fig. 6.1 shows an oxygen dissociation curve for adult human haemoglobin.
{{figure:figure_6_1.webp}}
Fig. 6.1
An increase in the partial pressure of carbon dioxide ($pCO_2$) in respiring tissue causes the Bohr effect.
parts.text: Sketch on Fig. 6.1 to show how the Bohr effect changes the oxygen dissociation curve.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Explain how an increase in $pCO_2$ produces the Bohr effect and state the benefit of this effect for the tissue.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Carbon dioxide ($CO_2$) is transported across the cell surface membrane of the red blood cell using a different mechanism to the transport of hydrogen carbonate ions ($HCO_3^-$).
Name the different mechanisms of transport used for $CO_2$ and for $HCO_3^-$ and explain why they are transported across the membrane by different mechanisms.
